title: Hepatitis A vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that protects against hepatitis A, a liver infection spread through dirty hands, water and food. Usually 2 shots are given.
why: For children and adults who are not vaccinated, before travel to hot countries, with liver disease, and in places with outbreaks.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes; the second shot is usually 6 to 12 months later
tell_doctor: If you are sick now or have a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines
If you already had hepatitis A

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are healthy. You will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: The course is usually 2 shots. Write down the date of the second.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes so the shoulder is easy to uncover.

steps: A doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, sit at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes the spot aches for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes weakness or a mild fever
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
You can go back to your usual activities
Do not forget the second shot
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a rash all over: call your local emergency number

faq.q: If I was in contact with a sick person, will the vaccine help?
faq.a: Often yes, if given quickly, usually within the first 2 weeks. See a doctor urgently.

faq.q: Does it protect against hepatitis B and C?
faq.a: No. There is a separate vaccine for hepatitis B, and none for C.

reminders.text: Hepatitis A vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
